task: Implement cryptographic and checksum algorithms (SHA-256, CRC-32, FNV-1a, LZ4 hash) using native bitwise operators.
observation: The newly merged native 64-bit bitwise operators (&, |, ^, ~, <<, >>) lowered cleanly to Rust and matched Fast Debug semantic execution. Wrapping 32-bit operations with & 4294967295 allowed direct implementation of full round transforms and table indexing without arithmetic XOR emulation.
impact: Allowed direct standards-compliant implementation of SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4), CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3), and Adler-32 (RFC 1950) with high performance and zero emulation overhead.
evidence: packages/hash/src/main.moss: full 64-round SHA-256 transform implemented using native bitwise operations
margo test: 5/5 tests passed in Native Debug, Fast Debug, and Native Release

resolution.summary: Utilized native Int bitwise operators directly with 32-bit truncation masks.

task: Define typed error enums for regex compilation and compression failures in raised error positions.
observation: Enum variants used in raise statements cannot contain heap-allocated String payloads in Moss v0.1 without causing lowering errors; only scalar bounded Int payloads are supported in raised error variants.
impact: Error types for RegexError, CompressError, and HashError had to be designed using numeric codes (such as character position or failure reason enum tag) rather than arbitrary diagnostic strings.
evidence: raise RegexError.InvalidSyntax(pos) succeeds with Int payload
raise RegexError.InvalidSyntax(msg) fails when msg is String

resolution.summary: Standardize raised error enum variants on integer error codes and token offset indices.
